subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Zero Trust Architecture
description: A short lesson to help you apply Zero Trust Architecture.

hook.text: Traditional security built a wall around the network. Once inside, everything was trusted. Attackers loved it.

buildup.text: Zero Trust assumes every user, device, and connection is potentially hostile — even those inside the network.

discovery.text: Google pioneered BeyondCorp after being hacked by China in 2010. It eliminated the trusted internal network.

twist.text: Implementing Zero Trust requires rebuilding identity, access, and monitoring from scratch. It takes years.

climax.text: Zero Trust is the future of security, but most organizations are still years away from full adoption.

punchline.text: Trust nothing. Verify everything. The new security model.

quiz.question: What is the core principle of Zero Trust?
options: Never trust any user or device by default
